newsitem.title: ITALY: Three Albanian patrol boats head for Italy.
newsitem.headline: Three Albanian patrol boats head for Italy.

text.p: Three Albanian navy patrol boats with an unknown number of people on board fled the country on Thursday and surrendered to an Italian frigate in the Adriatic, the Italian navy said.

It reported the incident as a merchant ship carrying scores of Albanians steamed towards southern Italy, apparently after crowds desperate to flee spreading insurgency in the Balkan state stormed the port of Durres and scrambled on board.
Last week, an Albanian MiG-15 plane landed in southern Italy and its two pilots asked for political asylum.
An Italian navy spokesman said the three patrol boats raised the white flag in international waters in the Adriatic after being sighted by the Italian frigate Aliseo.
They were being escorted to the southern port of Brindisi by an Italian navy corvette, the Danaide.
"Given that they are patrol boats, they would probably carry a total of 30 crew. But it could be that there are civilians on board," the spokesman said.
The merchant ship, which various reports said was carrying anywhere from 100 to 400 Albanians, was also being escorted to Brindisi by the Italian navy, coastguards said.
The Italian news agency ANSA named the ship as the St Vincent-registered "Giorgios".
The agency said the port of Durres was not officially closed but all ships had moved away from the harbour.

It quoted the captain of the Italian ferry Palladio, which set out from Durres for Bari on Thursday, as saying from on board that his ship had made a hurried departure as stone-throwing Albanians surged into the docks.
"The crucial moment came at 10.35 when we got orders over radio to cast off and get away fast. We did it as a ferocious crowd burst into the port," the captain, Ernesto Giardina, said.

Italy, which has taken an active role in international efforts to end Albania's deepening chaos, was hit by a wave of some 40,000 Albanians who fled in rusting freighters in 1991 after iron-fisted Stalinist rule collapsed in their country.
It has beefed up security in the southern Adriatic and Prime Minister Romano Prodi was meeting key ministers on Thursday for crisis talks on the latest developments in Albania.
The situation in Albania slid closer to anarchy on Thursday as arms depots in several towns including the capital Tirana were looted and food warehouses were raided.
Albanian President Sali Berisha and all political parties called on Thursday for NATO's European members to provide military assistance to Tirana to restore order.
Rebels have seized control of the south in an anti-government uprising sparked by anger over the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.
